dedupe_keys.name: enexis netbeheer open data small user consumption by postcode decentralised generation and congestion profile netherlands

description: Enexis Netbeheer, a Dutch regional grid operator, shares part of the energy data from its work as open data, free for anyone and anonymised so it cannot be traced to a person or a specific connection. Four data sets are offered: consumption of small-user connections per postcode area; aggregated decentralised generation of small-user connections in its service area; aggregated wind and solar generation per neighbourhood for large-user connections; and an example station profile for congestion management showing how often grid congestion can occur and how much power must be curtailed or redispatched. Each data set comes with an explanation of its meaning and currency, and some include history up to three years back, with older data on request from Partners in Energie. Users request the data sets with a form and receive them by email; the page states that the data may be used freely, subject to a disclaimer, and links to the outage site Energieonderbrekingen.nl, run with Liander and Stedin, and to grid operator area maps. Coverage is the Enexis service area. Caveats: data are aggregated by postcode or neighbourhood, key figures are no longer downloadable, and delivery is by email, not direct download. Simulation uses are local demand and distributed generation for distribution network and congestion studies. Related records: data-netherlands-grid-operator-service-areas maps which operator serves each area.
